topIssues.title: SDM: baseline benchmarks on sdm-net-0
topIssues.author: einar-oplabs
topIssues.body:
Perform the baseline benchmarks called for by #21273 on the now-live `sdm-net-0`, feeding #20176 (SDM performance benchmarking: execution, payload building, tracing/inspector path, `eth_getBlockReceipts` latency for `0x7d` blocks).

Notes from the rollout:
- The operator opt-in (`admin_setOperatorSdmOptIn`) is a runtime toggle → clean SDM-on vs SDM-off control arms on the same network without redeploys (re-arm after any sequencer restart)
- Follow the Benchmarking Hub SOP; sustained load prerequisite is tracked in the standing-workload sub-issue

Parent: #21273. Related: #20176.

topIssues.title: op-acceptance-tests: run TestSyncAfterInitialELSync against kona-node
topIssues.author: joshklop
topIssues.body:
## Summary

[`TestSyncAfterInitialELSync`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/develop/op-acceptance-tests/tests/sync/clsync/gap_clp2p/sync_test.go) is skipped when the acceptance suite runs against kona-node.

After out-of-order unsafe payload delivery, Kona does not advance the EL through the gap once the missing payload arrives.

## Required work

Reproduce and diagnose the unsafe-payload queue behavior, fix Kona or the test synchronization as appropriate, and remove the Kona skip.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The root cause and resolution are documented.
- [ ] `TestSyncAfterInitialELSync` no longer skips when `DEVSTACK_L2CL_KIND=kona-node`.
- [ ] Kona advances the EL through the filled unsafe gap and reaches the expected head.
- [ ] Existing op-node coverage continues to pass.

## Related

- https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/17694
- Parent inventory: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/protocol-team/issues/101

topIssues.title: [PCD] End-to-end integration test
topIssues.author: 0xOneTony
topIssues.body: Full pipeline against an Anvil L1 plus a real prestate builder, exercising every stage in order. Verifies that the deployed `DisputeGameFactory` has `CANNON` and `CANNON_KONA` configured with the expected prestate hashes, that `AnchorStateRegistry` on-chain holds the computed genesis output root, and that `op-node` produces L2 block 1 at the committed genesis timestamp. Includes a kill-and-resume scenario that interrupts the pipeline after each new stage and restarts it, confirming the skip conditions work in combination — unit tests catch them in isolation but not in interaction.

topIssues.title: [PCD] Idempotency wiring for new stages
topIssues.author: 0xOneTony
topIssues.body: The existing `op-deployer` pipeline survives partial failure by having each stage check whether its output is already present in state before running. The three new stages (predict L1 addresses, compute genesis output root, post-deploy validation) and the two moved stages (depset, prestate) all need the same treatment so a deploy that crashes mid-pipeline can be resumed without redoing completed work.

topPRs.title: op-deployer: share one bootstrapped L1 across PCD test cases
topPRs.author: maurelian
topPRs.body:
`TestCLIPCDResume` ran a full Anvil + `bootstrap superchain` + `bootstrap implementations` for each of its nine cases, and `TestCLIPCDJourney` for each of its two. The bootstrap pair is the slowest op-deployer operation and nothing under test mutates it, so it now runs once per test function.

`pcdBootstrappedL1` holds the bootstrapped L1 and hands each case a fresh CLI runner and workdir on it. `newJourney` first reverts the L1 to a post-bootstrap snapshot, restoring the deployer nonce, block height, and any injected code — so the existing absolute-nonce assertions and `postBootstrapL1State` baseline hold unchanged, and rerunning a failed case is now idempotent.

`TestCLIPCDBoot` keeps its own L1; it needs a Prague-specific Anvil.

Measured locally, same synthetic prestate for both runs:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `TestCLIPCDResume` | 398.9s | 95.6s |
| `TestCLIPCDJourney` | 89.7s | 51.1s |

That is ~5.7 min off the `go-tests` shard, which runs this package under a 40m budget.

Targets `test/pcd-e2e-integration` (#22356).

**Description**

Adds end-to-end tests for the staged PCD CLI against a local Anvil L1. The tests cover:

- One-chain and two-chain super-root deployments
- Restarting from the saved work directory at each stage boundary and after `continue` failures

Only super-root games are tested because current OPCMs reject legacy game types. The permissioned fallback is checked as configuration only.

The tests use the prestate hash built by CI.

topPRs.title: feat: Keccak256 alt-DA without a challenge contract + op-supernode HTTP remote interop nodes
topPRs.author: opsuperchain
topPRs.body:
This combines two previously-drafted features into the minimal "bones" of a private alt-DA chain that interops one-way with external finalized chains: keccak-committed alt-DA with no challenge contract, plus a way for a supernode to treat an external chain as a read-only member of its interop dependency set. Neither half is new work on its own — the point of putting them in one branch is that the combination is what a permissioned Validium that wants to read finalized messages from a public chain actually needs, and it is worth seeing the seam between them. Opened as a **draft for visibility and discussion, not for merge**.

## Commits

**1. `feat(op-alt-da): allow Keccak256 commitments without DAChallengeAddress`**

A revival of #19395 by @fakedev9999 (preserved as the commit author). It makes the DA challenge contract optional for Keccak256 commitments, so a permissioned Validium can keep the `keccak256(data) == commitment` verify-on-read that generic commitments give up, without standing up a challenge game. The guard on `fetchChallengeLogs` moves from commitment-type-based to address-based: challenge machinery is skipped exactly when `da_challenge_contract_address` is zero, and is untouched otherwise.

It also fixes the two op-node alt-DA derive tests that #19395 broke. `TestAltDADataSourceStall` and `TestAltDADataSourceInvalidData` build an `altda.Config` with no challenge contract address, so under the address-based guard the manager skips challenge-log lookups and the tests fail on unmet `FetchReceipts` expectations. They now get an explicit non-zero test challenge contract, so they keep exercising the challenge flow they were written for rather than being weakened.

**2. `feat(op-supernode): HTTP-backed remote interop nodes`**

A revival of draft #21479 (original author and co-author preserved). It adds a *remote node*: a member of the interop dependency set that the supernode does not drive. Rather than running a consensus client for that chain, the supernode polls an HTTP endpoint for its **finalized** initiating messages and seals them into that chain's LogsDB, so driven chains can reference them as executing messages exactly as they reference driven-chain messages. Finalized-only means there is no rewind path to implement. The wire protocol is the plugin boundary — `GET {url}/finalized?after={N}` — so the far side can be any server in any language; configured with `--interop.remote-nodes <chainID>=<url>`.

New in this branch, all of it forced by running the thing against a live public chain:

- **Start-height anchoring.** #21479 resumed from the LogsDB's latest sealed block and demanded strict contiguity from there, with an empty DB meaning "expect block 1" — unreachable for a chain whose finalized head is tens of millions of blocks past genesis. An empty LogsDB now accepts whatever height the adapter serves for `after=0` and seals it as the anchor of local history; contiguity is enforced from the anchor onward exactly as before. Nothing below the DB layer changed — the raft-wal store already keys by block number and records its own first block — and this mirrors how a driven chain's logsDB already starts at an arbitrary height via `--interop.log-backfill-depth`.
- **Ingestion drain with a per-cycle cap.** Ingestion ran once per tick and the tick is the remote chain's block time, so it could only ever match the chain's production rate; a node that fell behind on a 2s chain could never catch up. The loop now drains until the adapter returns null, capped per cycle to keep shutdown responsive and bound adapter load.
- **An env-gated live e2e** exercising the whole chain of custody — real server process against a real public chain, real `HTTPAdapter`, real ingester, real LogsDB — ending by asking `Contains` for a genuine on-chain log with the checksum an executing message would carry. Anchors at the wrong height, a logHash derived differently on the two sides, a log index shifted by a filtered log: none of those are visible in a test with fabricated blocks.

## Validation

Beyond the unit and engine-level tests, this exact combination was deployed as a live chain on Sepolia and exercised end to end: deposits through the portal, alt-DA keccak batch derivation with no challenge contract, live executing messages referencing **finalized OP Sepolia logs** delivered over the remote-node path, and withdrawals proven and finalized through super-root permissioned dispute games. No infrastructure or endpoint details are included here.

## Known gaps / future work

- The remote-node protocol has **no auth and no handshake**. It is a trusted-endpoint plugin seam as it stands; anything adversarial needs authentication and probably a version/chain-ID negotiation on connect.
- **Interop tx filter integration** is future work: admission-time validation of transactions whose executing messages reference a remote chain is served by a separate service, which does not know about remote nodes yet. Today the remote path is validated at block-building/verification time only.
- The test impact of #19395 is fixed in commit 1 rather than left for a follow-up, since the two commits are meant to be reviewable independently.

topPRs.title: op-dispute-mon: extract and forecast ZK games
topPRs.author: wwared
topPRs.body:
## Claim

Extract complete non-bond ZK snapshots at one pinned L1 block and deterministically reconcile, cache, and forecast them while keeping production ZK caller creation disabled.

## Base and dependency

PR 3 of 5. Base: `feat/zk-monitor-fault-bonds`; depends on #22226. PRs 3–5 form the ZK landing cohort; this PR is inert in production until PR 5.

Stack order: #22225 → #22226 → #22227 → #22228 → #22229.

## Commits and reading order

1. `25801f0af1` adds the minimal pinned binding reads and checked proposal-status conversion.
2. `b4fc4fa8bd` adds ZK agreement, extraction, cache behavior, and forecast routing.

## Review focus

- The binding reads establish that parent status, metadata, participants, and anchor registry all use the requested block.
- The state machine runs the lag gate before later reads and preserves three outcomes: lagged-new omitted, lagged-cached retained without failure, and real-RPC-failing cached retained with failure.
- The literal proposal/agreement/parent decision tables route ZK only to the common lane. `GameCallerCreator.CreateContract` still rejects ZK.

## Intentional behavior changes

- Out-of-sync endpoints are subtracted from successful endpoints when evaluating mixed availability, preventing a lagged ZK source from being reported as available.
- Existing Fault and SuperPermissioned behavior remains unchanged.

## Tests

- `mise exec -- go test ./op-challenger/game/fault/contracts ./op-challenger/game/zk ./op-dispute-mon/... -count=1`
- `mise exec -- just lint-go`

topPRs.title: op-devstack: Wait for the destination chain before sending executing messages
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
An executing message whose block predates the initiating message it references is invalid, so consolidation replaces the block. Nothing waited for the destination chain to catch up before submitting the exec tx, so whenever it lagged the source chain the test got a replaced block.

That is what failed `TestInteropFaultProofs_DepositMessage/SP1NativeCore` on [pipeline 131101](https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/github/ethereum-optimism/optimism/131101/workflows/e0ef036d-80b8-44fc-b399-9faa9abbbd17/jobs/5377289): chain B sequenced the exec message into a block at ts 1785190016 while the init log on chain A was at ts 1785190020, and the supernode invalidated it — `initiating timestamp 1785190020 > executing timestamp 1785190016` — leaving one optimistic root replaced where the checkpoint expected none.

Every path that submits an executing message now waits for the destination chain to build past the initiating timestamp:

- `EOA.SendExecMessage`, `SendInvalidExecMessage`, `SendPackedExecMessages`, `PrepareExecTx`
- `EOA.WaitForInitMessages` is exported for the tests that build exec txs with `txintent` directly (`interop/message`, `interop/reorgs`)
- `interopsmoke` hits the same race against live chains, so `remoteUser` waits too

The wait is strict (`initTs + 1`), matching the interop load test, which already did this inline: op-geth filters pending executing messages against the unsafe head timestamp rather than the pending block ([op-geth#603](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/issues/603)).

Not changed: `SameTimestampPair.SubmitExecTo` / `SubmitExecForMessage`. Those reference precomputed identifiers for blocks the test sequencer has not built yet, so there is nothing to wait for.

## Test plan

All with a local `op-reth`:

- `./tests/interop/message/` — full package, PASS (180s). Covers all six raw `txintent` sites plus `TestRandomDirectedGraph` via `SendPackedExecMessages`.
- `./tests/interop/reorgs/ -run TestReorgInitExecMsg` — PASS (45s).
- `./tests/supernode/interop/ -run TestSupernodeInteropBidirectionalMessages` — PASS (33s).

The guard was confirmed to act on real values, not to be a no-op: instrumented, `TestInitExecMsg` logged `initTs=1785192212 headTs=1785192214`; with the target temporarily forced to `initTs + 20`, the wait blocked until the chain reached it (head `initTs+20`, runtime 17.7s -> 35.9s) and the test still passed.
